content: 1. Nelfinavir can significantly increase or decrease estrogen plasma levels by affecting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, leading to increased levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol. This may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. It is recommended to avoid nelfinavir or use an alternative drug. 2. Nevirapine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended during coadministration. 3. Omaveloxolone decreases the levels or effects of both ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel transdermal by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives, including pills, patches, rings, implants, and progestin-only pills. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 4. Oxcarbazepine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 5. Tovorafenib decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel transdermal by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with hormonal contraceptives. If unavoidable, use additional effective nonhormonal contraceptive methods during coadministration and for 28 days after discontinuation. 6. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of albiglutide through pharmacodynamic antagonism, potentially impairing glycemic control in diabetic patients. Monitor glycemic control closely. 7. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of alosetron by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of alprazolam by decreasing its metabolism. This may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, increasing serum concentrations. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Concomitant use of ethinyl estradiol and aminocaproic acid may lead to additive hypercoagulability. Estrogens increase clotting factor production and platelet aggregation, while aminocaproic acid inhibits fibrinolysis and plasminogen activity. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Amoxicillin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora, which applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 11. Ampicillin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora, which applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 12. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of atogepant by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Atorvastatin increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels of axitinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels of bendamustine by decreasing its metabolism. Bendamustine is minimally metabolized by CYP1A2, and ethinyl estradiol, a weak CYP1A2 inhibitor, may increase plasma concentrations of bendamustine. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of caffeine by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Cephalosporins (e.g., cefaclor, cefadroxil, cefazolin, cefdinir, cefepime, cefixime, cefotaxime, cefprozil, ceftazidime, ceftibuten, cefuroxime, cephalexin) decrease the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 19. Cenobamate decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel transdermal by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Women should use additional or alternative nonhormonal birth control methods during cenobamate use. 20. Combined oral contraceptives containing ethinyl estradiol may inhibit the metabolism of cyclosporine, increasing its plasma concentrations. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Ceritinib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Chloramphenicol decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 23. Cimetidine increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Ciprofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 25. Clarithromycin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 26. Clindamycin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 27. Clobazam decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended during coadministration. 28. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of clonazepam by decreasing its metabolism. This may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, increasing serum concentrations. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels of cyclosporine by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Dabrafenib decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 31. Danicopan increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by increasing plasma concentrations of BCRP substrates. Consider dose reduction of BCRP substrates as per prescribing information. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Darunavir decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Use nonhormonal contraceptive methods. 33. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of dasatinib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Deferasirox decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Demeclocycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 36. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of diazepam by decreasing its metabolism. This may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, increasing serum concentrations. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Dicloxacillin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 38. Doxycycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 39. Elafibranor decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol and levonorgestrel transdermal by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Switch to effective nonhormonal contraceptives or add a barrier method during elafibranor treatment and for at least 3 weeks after the last dose. 40. Elagolix decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor CYP3A substrates if coadministered and consider increasing the dose of CYP3A substrates if needed. 41. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel transdermal by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Ethinyl estradiol increases the levels or effects of eltrombopag by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 44. Encorafenib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting BCRP. Monitor for signs of increased exposure and consider adjusting the dose of BCRP substrates. 45. Erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, stearate) decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 46. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. The efficacy of hormonal contraceptives may be reduced. Use nonhormonal contraceptive methods.
